papers.title: Investigating the Local and Global Tensile Deformation Characteristics of Metallic Specimens Produced by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: Abstract Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) enables the production of highly customized components with intricate geometries for real-world applications. However, such complexity often introduces notches or stress concentrators that can significantly impact mechanical performance such as tensile properties. As a result, understanding of the tensile behavior of notched L-PBF components is crucial to fully exploiting L-PBF’s potential in structural and load-bearing applications. In this study, notched specimens of Hastelloy X and Ti-6Al-4V are fabricated using L-PBF and subjected to tensile testing at 72 °F and 500 °F. Both local and global tensile properties are examined. The results reveal that local stress values are higher than global stress for both alloys. At elevated temperatures, both alloys exhibit reduced tensile strength and increased elongation. Digital image correlation shows significantstrain localization around the notches at room temperature, with Hastelloy X displaying a more uniform strain distribution compared to the asymmetric pattern observed in Ti-6Al-4V, likely due to rough surfaces near the notch. Hastelloy X also demonstrates significantly higher total elongation, both locally and globally, than Ti-6Al-4V, although it exhibits lower yield and ultimate strength. Microstructural analysis reveals that Hastelloy X specimens have a larger grain size than Ti-6Al-4V, which, in addition to post-processing, notch, and surface finish, potentially contributes to the observed differences in tensile properties.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及Ti-6Al-4V的拉伸性能，但未具体研究后处理工艺（如热处理、HIP等）的影响。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not focus on any specific post-processing treatment; it examines the tensile behavior of notched as-built specimens, with only a passing mention of post-processing as a potential factor.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究L-PBF制备的含缺口金属试样的拉伸变形行为。
summary_zh.method: 对Hastelloy X和Ti-6Al-4V缺口试样进行室温和高温拉伸测试，并用数字图像相关分析应变分布。
summary_zh.result: 局部应力高于全局应力，高温降低强度但增加延伸率，Ti-6Al-4V应变分布不对称。
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸实验和微观结构分析验证。

summary_en.motivation: To understand the tensile deformation behavior of notched metallic specimens produced by laser powder bed fusion.
summary_en.method: Notched specimens of Hastelloy X and Ti-6Al-4V were tensile tested at 72 °F and 500 °F with digital image correlation to assess local and global strains.
summary_en.result: Local stresses exceeded global stresses for both alloys; elevated temperature reduced strength and increased elongation, with Ti-6Al-4V showing asymmetric strain localization.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through experimental tensile testing, DIC, and microstructural analysis.

papers.title: Beyond expert intuition: evaluating a vector‑adaptive scan strategy to enhance geometric fidelity in hard‑to‑print Ti‑6Al‑4V thin‑walled structures
papers.abstract: Abstract The fabrication of metallic thin-walled structures (TWS) via laser-based powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M) presents significant challenges in maintaining geometric fidelity and minimizing defects, both of which are strongly influenced by the laser scan strategy. This study introduces and empirically benchmarks a novel vector-adaptive scan strategy (Free Float) against conventional methods for producing dense TWS. The adaptive strategy dynamically modulates hatch vector number, length, and orientation in response to local geometry—specifically wall thickness and inclination angle—to control scanned area per layer and actively mitigate deleterious thermal gradients. A full-factorial design comprising 300 titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V) specimens, spanning ten wall thicknesses (0.1–1.0 mm), ten inclination angles (0°–90°), and three scan strategies were executed. Results demonstrate that the vector-adaptive strategy enhanced dimensional accuracy, particularly for critical shallow overhangs (10°–30°). It reduced average dimensional deviation by 29.7–30.6% compared to a standard strategy and by 3.5–3.7% relative to surface-optimized strategy with down-skin parameter adaptation. Specimens with wall thickness ≥ 0.2 mm achieved high structural integrity, with relative densities exceeding 98.65%. This work establishes a quantitative benchmark for adaptive scanning in PBF-LB/M, confirming its potential for fabricating high-integrity lightweight components.

summary_en.motivation: To improve the geometric fidelity of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V thin-walled structures.
summary_en.method: A novel vector-adaptive scan strategy (Free Float) was introduced and benchmarked against conventional methods.
summary_en.result: The adaptive strategy reduced dimensional deviation by up to 30.6% and achieved relative densities exceeding 98.65%.
summary_en.validation: A full-factorial experiment with 300 Ti-6Al-4V specimens spanning thicknesses and angles was conducted.
